    VLSplat: Vision-Language Guided Object-Centric 3D Gaussian Splatting via Scene Graph      

VLSplat Vision-Language Guided Object-Centric 3D Gaussian Splatting via Scene Graph
===================================================================================

NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight✨

[Yuntae Jeon](https://yuntaej.github.io/)1\* [Younho Jeon](https://iamyouno.github.io/)2\* Sujin Jin1 Sungho Jo2† Seunghee Park1†

1Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) 2Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

\*Equal contribution  ·  †Corresponding authors

[Paper](#) [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01939) [Code](https://github.com/yuntaeJ/VLSplat)

Abstract
--------

Learning semantic representations for 3D Gaussian Splatting has recently emerged as a promising direction for 3D scene understanding. However, existing 2D-to-3D semantic lifting approaches rely primarily on 2D segmentation supervision and lack object-level priors, causing the learned representation to be driven by local mask evidence rather than holistic object structure. In this paper, we present **VLSplat**, a vision-language guided approach for object-centric semantic lifting in 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our method augments mask-based lifting with object-level semantic priors derived from vision-language models and refines Gaussian representations using an object-group scene graph. The refinement is performed through two language-guided modules: _intra-group refinement_ suppresses semantic noise within object groups, while _inter-group acquisition_ expands object support regions by incorporating structurally relevant candidates from neighboring groups. Extensive experiments on indoor scene datasets demonstrate that VLSplat improves semantic consistency and structural completeness.

Method
------

![Overview of VLSplat](static/images/overview.webp)

**Overview.** VLSplat lifts object-aware 2D masks into an object-level Gaussian codebook, reinterprets codebook groups as nodes of a **scene graph** with VLM-generated object descriptions, and refines each object with **CLIP-guided Gaussian gating**. The semantic representation and scene graph are updated iteratively throughout 3DGS optimization.

1

### Codebook-based semantic lifting

Hybrid SAM3 (text-prompted) + SAM2 masks supervise Gaussian features associated with an object-level codebook, giving coarse object groups.

2

### Scene graph as object prior

Each group becomes a node with an anisotropic-connectivity ROI, a category and a VLM-generated object description; overlapping ROIs form edges.

3

### Object-centric refinement

Intra-node refinement removes noisy Gaussians; inter-node acquisition recovers missing parts from neighbors — both decided by CLIP-guided gates on synthetic object views.

![Vision-language-guided object-centric refinement](static/images/refinement.webp)

**Language-guided Gaussian gating.** Candidate Gaussians receive learnable gates; the gates maximize the CLIP-similarity _gain_ of the gated rendering over the reliable-core rendering. High-gate candidates are attracted to the node prototype, low-gate ones are repelled — geometry is left untouched.

[](#vlsplat)

### Vision-Language Guided Object-Centric 3D Gaussian Splatting via Scene Graph

[](#vision-language-guided-object-centric-3d-gaussian-splatting-via-scene-graph)

[Project Page](https://vlsplat.github.io/)

VLSplat lifts 2D semantic masks into object-centric 3D Gaussian groups and refines them with object-level language priors organized as a scene graph. A codebook associates Gaussians into object groups; each group becomes a graph node carrying a class, a VLM-written description, and a 3D box. Two refinement stages then run under CLIP guidance on synthetic object views — _intra-node_ suppresses noisy Gaussians inside a node, _inter-node_ acquires missing parts from neighbouring or background nodes — updating features only, never geometry.

Code Structure
--------------

[](#code-structure)

    VLSplat/
    ├── 1_train_15k.sh                 stage 1  codebook lifting
    ├── 2_init_scene_graph.sh          stage 2  scene graph + VLM prompts
    ├── 3_train_15k_30k.sh             stage 3  intra/inter refinement
    ├── test_vlsplat_2d_render.sh      eval     render-level (VLSplat)
    ├── test_unified-lift_2d_render.sh eval     render-level (baseline)
    ├── test_vlsplat_3d_point.sh       eval     point-level
    ├── train_vlsplat.py               training loop
    ├── config/                        one config per setup (paths, training mode, graph and refinement settings)
    ├── preprocess/                    stage 0  SAM3 + SAM2 masks (run_masks.sh)
    ├── scene_graph_builder/           scene graph: construction (step 2), per-cycle refinement and last-step finalize (step 3)
    ├── clip_refine/                   synthetic object views + CLIP gating
    ├── script/                        evaluation (and the Unified-Lift eval graph)
    ├── scene/ gaussian_renderer/ utils/ arguments/    3DGS core
    └── submodules/                    diff-gaussian-rasterization, simple-knn
    

Installation
------------

[](#installation)

Python 3.8, PyTorch 2.4.1, CUDA 12.1, gcc/g++ 12, one GPU with ≥ 24 GB.

conda create -n vlsplat python=3.8 -y
conda activate vlsplat

pip install torch==2.4.1 torchvision==0.19.1 torchaudio==2.4.1 \\
    --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
pip install plyfile==0.8.1 tqdm scipy wandb opencv-python scikit-learn lpips open\_clip\_torch

CC=gcc-12 CXX=g++-12 pip install submodules/diff-gaussian-rasterization --no-build-isolation
pip install submodules/simple-knn --no-build-isolation

export OPENROUTER\_API\_KEY='sk-or-...'   # VLM of step 2

Mask preprocessing uses a separate `sam3` environment (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.10, CUDA 12.8):

conda create -n sam3 python=3.12 pip -y
conda activate sam3
pip install torch==2.10.0 torchvision==0.25.0 \\
    --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128

git clone https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3.git preprocess/sam3/sam3
git clone https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam2.git preprocess/sam2/sam2

SAM2\_BUILD\_CUDA=0 pip install --no-build-isolation \\
    -e preprocess/sam3/sam3 -e preprocess/sam2/sam2 \\
    -r preprocess/requirements.txt \\
    'setuptools<81' 'opencv-python<4.12' scipy matplotlib

mkdir -p preprocess/sam3/weights preprocess/sam2/weights
hf auth login    # access to facebook/sam3 required
hf download facebook/sam3 sam3.pt --local-dir preprocess/sam3/weights
curl -fL --retry 3 \\
    https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/segment\_anything\_2/092824/sam2.1\_hiera\_large.pt \\
    -o preprocess/sam2/weights/sam2.1\_hiera\_large.pt

Data
----

[](#data)

Place each scene under `data/<dataset>/<scene>/` (`<dataset>` = `scannetpp`, `scannetv2`, ...); a symlink works: `ln -s /path/to/datasets data`.

**Input (before preprocessing)**

    data/<dataset>/<scene>/
    ├── images/                RGB frames
    ├── sparse/0/              COLMAP model (cameras, images, points3D)
    ├── train_test_lists.json  render protocol: train/test split
    └── gt/
        ├── render/            render protocol: semantic index PNGs, one per test view
        └── points/            point protocol: *_vh_clean_2.labels.ply, *.aggregation.json, *.segs.json
    

### Preprocessing

[](#preprocessing)

conda activate sam3
DATASET=scannetpp SCENE=8b5caf3398 bash preprocess/run\_masks.sh
DATASET=scannetv2 SCENE=scene0590\_00 bash preprocess/run\_masks.sh

**Output (new folders next to `images/`)**

    data/<dataset>/<scene>/
    ├── object_mask/           per-image object-ID masks, used for training
    ├── object_mask_json/      per-image label of each mask ID (SAM3 class, or SAM2 fill)
    └── object_mask_vis/       colour visualizations for inspection
    

Training outputs go to `output/<dataset>/<scene>/<run>/`.

Training and Inference
----------------------

[](#training-and-inference)

### VLSplat (render-level)

[](#vlsplat-render-level)

conda activate vlsplat
export DATASET\_CONFIG=vlsplat\_render\_scannetpp SCENE=8b5caf3398   # config/vlsplat\_render\_scannetpp.py

bash 1\_train\_15k.sh          # → base\_15k
bash 2\_init\_scene\_graph.sh   # → base\_15k/point\_cloud/iteration\_15000/scene\_graph\_sam3\_vlm.json
bash 3\_train\_15k\_30k.sh      # → vlsplat\_30k (final graph: point\_cloud/iteration\_30000/scene\_graph.json)

Without an OpenRouter key, export `PIPELINE_VARIANT=sam3` before steps 2 and 3 (SAM3 votes only, no VLM).

Unified-Lift baseline (reuses the same 15k checkpoint):

DATASET\_CONFIG=unified\_lift+ours\_scannetpp bash 3\_train\_15k\_30k.sh   # → unified\_lift\_30k

### VLSplat (point-level)

[](#vlsplat-point-level)

export DATASET\_CONFIG=vlsplat\_point\_scannetv2 SCENE=scene0590\_00   # config/vlsplat\_point\_scannetv2.py

bash 1\_train\_15k.sh          # → base\_15k\_fixed
bash 2\_init\_scene\_graph.sh
bash 3\_train\_15k\_30k.sh      # → vlsplat\_30k\_fixed

Evaluation
----------

[](#evaluation)

SCENE=8b5caf3398 bash test\_vlsplat\_2d\_render.sh        # render-level
SCENE=8b5caf3398 bash test\_unified-lift\_2d\_render.sh   # render-level baseline
SCENE=scene0590\_00 bash test\_vlsplat\_3d\_point.sh       # point-level

Acknowledgements
----------------

[](#acknowledgements)

Built on [3D Gaussian Splatting](https://github.com/graphdeco-inria/gaussian-splatting) and [Unified-Lift](https://github.com/Runsong123/Unified-Lift), with masks from [SAM2](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam2) / [SAM3](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3) and language features from [OpenCLIP](https://github.com/mlfoundations/open_clip). Please follow the original 3D Gaussian Splatting license terms, which restrict use to non-commercial research.

**What it does:** It lifts 2D object masks into a 3DGS "codebook" of object groups. Each group becomes a node in a scene graph with a class, a VLM-written description, and a 3D box. Two CLIP-guided refinement stages then clean the groups. Intra-node refinement removes noisy Gaussians. Inter-node acquisition adds missing parts from neighbouring nodes. The README says these stages update features only, never geometry. Output is semantic, not RGB-only.

**Inputs:**
- Per-scene COLMAP model required: `sparse/0/` with cameras, images, points3D. So poses are needed (not pose-free).
- RGB frames in `images/`, plus `train_test_lists.json` for the render protocol.
- Number of views, video support, and resolution: not stated in any of the three sources.
- Maximum frame count: not stated.

**Outputs:**
- Per-image object-ID masks (`object_mask/`), mask labels (`object_mask_json/`), and visualizations.
- Training output goes to `output/<dataset>/<scene>/<run>/`, with `point_cloud/iteration_15000/scene_graph_sam3_vlm.json` and `point_cloud/iteration_30000/scene_graph.json` in the README.
- Trained 3DGS checkpoints, using the 3DGS-style `point_cloud/` layout. The README never says "PLY". I did not confirm the Gaussian file format.
- Semantic features: yes (codebook features, scene graph, CLIP-based features). Not RGB-only.

**Quality numbers (project page tables, column headers garbled in extraction, so verify before citing):**
- Render-level segmentation (mAcc/mIoU, Thing/Stuff). VLSplat on ScanNet++ is listed as 70.31 / 74.09 / 69.81 / 67.79. On Replica it is 68.69 / 68.11 / 68.59 / 67.75. Baselines in the same table include LangSplatV2, OpenGaussian, and LEGaussian.

A "†" localized variant reaches 61.89 / 79.12 / 46.18 / 27.80 on ScanNetV2. PanoGS, which the page compares against, scores 54.50 / 74.98 / 35.65 / 30.32 on ScanNetV2 and is higher on mIoU for that dataset.
- Datasets: ScanNet++ (scene `8b5caf3398`), ScanNetV2 (scene `scene0590_00`), Replica. The README names no other datasets.

**Single-scene or feed-forward:** Single-scene optimization. Each scene is trained separately. Stage 1 is 15k iterations, stage 3 runs to 30k. No feed-forward model is described.

**Code and weights:**
- Code: released on GitHub under `yuntaeJ/VLSplat`, public, 4 commits, 5 stars, 1 fork.
- Pretrained weights: not found. The arXiv abstract says "Our code and models are available" at the project URL. The repo has no weights link, no Releases, and no model files in the listing. The weights are SAM2/SAM3 downloads, not VLSplat's own.

- Main environment: Python 3.8, PyTorch 2.4.1, CUDA 12.1, gcc/g++ 12, one GPU with at least 24 GB.
- Mask preprocessing (separate env): Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.10, CUDA 12.8.

CC=gcc-12 CXX=g++-12 pip install submodules/diff-gaussian-rasterization --no-build-isolation
pip install submodules/simple-knn --no-build-isolation
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY='REDACTED'
```

DATASET=scannetpp SCENE=8b5caf3398 bash preprocess/run_masks.sh
```
```
conda activate vlsplat
export DATASET_CONFIG=vlsplat_render_scannetpp SCENE=8b5caf3398
bash 1_train_15k.sh
bash 2_init_scene_graph.sh
bash 3_train_15k_30k.sh
```

- Gaussian PLY format and export details.

VLSplat: Vision-Language Guided Object-Centric 3D Gaussian Splatting via Scene Graph (Jeon, Jeon, Jin, Jo, Park; SKKU and KAIST; NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight per the project page).

Sources read: https://vlsplat.github.io/ (project page), https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01939 (v1, submitted 1 Nov 2026), https://github.com/yuntaeJ/VLSplat (README and file listing).

What it does: lifts 2D object masks into a 3DGS "codebook" of object groups. Each group becomes a scene-graph node with a class, a VLM-written description, and a 3D box. Two CLIP-guided refinement stages clean the groups: intra-node refinement removes noisy Gaussians; inter-node acquisition adds missing parts from neighbouring nodes. The README says these stages update features only, never geometry. Output is semantic, not RGB-only.

Inputs:
- Per-scene COLMAP model required (sparse/0/: cameras, images, points3D). So poses are needed; not pose-free.
- RGB frames in images/, plus train_test_lists.json for the render protocol.
- Number of views, video support, resolution, and frame limit: not stated in any of the three sources.

Outputs:
- Per-image object-ID masks (object_mask/), mask labels (object_mask_json/), visualizations (object_mask_vis/).
- Training output in output/<dataset>/<scene>/<run>/, e.g. point_cloud/iteration_15000/scene_graph_sam3_vlm.json and point_cloud/iteration_30000/scene_graph.json.
- Trained 3DGS checkpoints in a 3DGS-style point_cloud/ layout. The README never says "PLY"; Gaussian file format not confirmed.
